reasons: Lake identity gives record_id/input_case_name United States v. Vasquez-Algarin, court 3d Cir. 2016, decided 2016-05-02, docket 15-1941.
Lake citations list official cite 821 F.3d 467 and vendor-neutral cites 2016 U.S. App. LEXIS 7889 and 2016 WL 1730540; lake parallel citations are empty.
The opinion frames the question as how certain officers must be that a suspect resides at and is present at an address before forcing entry into a private dwelling.
The opinion discusses Payton and Steagald in-home arrest rules and forced entry to execute an arrest warrant, supporting placement under Arrest in the Home as a key case.
The opinion states: "we join the Fifth, Sixth, Seventh and Ninth Circuits in holding that Payton’s “reason to believe” language amounts to a probable cause standard."
The opinion further states officers must have probable cause to believe the suspect "resides at and is present within the dwelling before making a forced entry."

On application, the court held law enforcement did not meet probable cause as to either Payton prong and concluded: "we will reverse the District Court’s denial of Vasquez-Algarin’s motion to suppress, vacate the conviction, and remand."
residual_risks: The opinion notes caveats that the Seventh Circuit had only inclined toward the view and the Sixth Circuit endorsement was dictum, but the Third Circuit itself still phrased its holding as joining those circuits.
